analysis.report_markdown:
## 1. Executive Summary

BrickByte provides weekly drone scans compared with BIM models to track construction progress and catch deviations early, targeting developers, contractors and construction lenders in India. The startup has 23 paying customers across 61 active sites, generating an ARR of Rs 1.3 crore (FY2026, company-reported and unverified) with a net revenue retention of 126% and monthly churn of 1.5% [c:towvifa][c:nkfzqiz]. The team of three co-founders brings relevant domain experience in civil engineering, photogrammetry, and drone operations [c:uifebyv]. The company is raising Rs 6 crore at a Rs 32 crore pre-money valuation, with a tranche-based structure tied to milestones of 150 active sites and Rs 3 crore ARR [c:r542uqa]. Key risks include reliance on real-estate cycles, drone regulations, operations-heavy margins, and limited BIM adoption among Indian developers [c:q6ewrkd]. Overall score: 5.6/10, recommendation: Hold.

## 2. Problem & Solution

Developers, contractors and lenders learn about construction delays and deviations weeks late because progress reporting is manual and hard to verify. BrickByte estimates that manual progress reports lag site reality by 2-4 weeks and that large Indian real-estate projects frequently overrun schedules [c:4kixigp]. BrickByte’s solution is automated weekly drone flights by certified remote pilots, turning imagery into 3D models compared with BIM to flag deviations by floor and element, and providing progress against schedule and quantity estimates for billing checks [c:677mkuk]. The service also delivers independent progress reports for construction lenders [c:677mkuk].

## 3. Market Opportunity

BrickByte estimates the TAM for construction progress-monitoring and reality-capture software in India at Rs 1,600 crore in 2025, the SAM at Rs 300 crore scoped to five cities (NCR, Mumbai, Pune, Bengaluru, Hyderabad), and the SOM at Rs 14 crore by 2029 [c:uypjwak]. All figures are company-reported and unverified; no independent third-party sizing or publisher forecasts are provided. The market is sizable and clearly defined, but the lack of external validation and the reliance on company projections cap the market score at 5.0.

## 4. Competitive Landscape

BrickByte’s competitive edge is a BIM-comparison engine tuned for Indian construction methods and a growing dataset across 61 sites that improves delay prediction [c:2lspiuh]. Competitors include Procore (global construction-management software, which acquired DroneDeploy to bring visual intelligence to jobsites) [w:8][w:10], Skylark Drones (Indian drone-data platform for surveys and infrastructure, Series A, raised $4.58M) [w:14][w:15], and manual site reports using spreadsheets and photos [c:2lspiuh]. The deck’s positioning is execution-based rather than defensible; competitors can replicate similar capabilities, and no IP protection or network effects are cited.

## 5. Business Model

Revenue comes from per-site subscriptions at Rs 18,000 per month (88% of revenue) and lender progress reports at Rs 45,000 per report (12% of revenue) [c:j4xook5]. ARR counts only site subscriptions. Unit economics: gross margin 64%, customer acquisition cost Rs 250,000, CAC payback 8.2 months, net revenue retention 126%, monthly churn 1.5% [c:nkfzqiz]. The payback period is above the 6-month threshold for a higher score, and early data is positive but not yet proven at scale. The business model is clear and the unit economics are disclosed, supporting a score of 6.0.

## 6. Team Assessment

The three co-founders have relevant domain and execution experience: Kunal Sethi (CEO) is a civil engineer with 9 years in project planning at a large NCR developer; Ritu Choudhary (CTO) is a photogrammetry and computer-vision engineer who built 3D reconstruction pipelines; Gaurav Bhatia (COO) ran drone-survey operations for mining and infrastructure clients [c:uifebyv]. This is a complete founding team with good domain fit, but none have prior startup founding or scaling experience at a proven high-growth company. The team scores 6.0.

## 7. Traction & Milestones

BrickByte has grown ARR from Rs 0.2 crore (FY2024) to Rs 0.6 crore (FY2025) to Rs 1.3 crore (FY2026), representing ~2x year-over-year growth [c:towvifa]. The company serves 23 paying customers across 61 active sites in NCR, Pune, and Hyderabad, with a net revenue retention (NRR) of 126% as customers add sites [c:towvifa]. It has also sold progress-verification reports to 2 construction lenders, a secondary revenue stream [c:towvifa]. Unit economics show a gross margin of 64%, CAC of Rs 250,000, CAC payback of 8.2 months, and monthly churn of 1.5% [c:nkfzqiz]. All traction figures are company-reported and unverified.

## 8. Compliance & Governance

The MCA registry confirms BrickByte Private Limited (CIN U71100HR2023PTC113592) is ACTIVE, with directors Kunal Sethi, Ritu Choudhary, and Gaurav Bhatia [c:fys5mnw]. No compliance flags were raised. The deck does not attempt to instruct the evaluator. The company operates under India's DGCA drone regulations, which require registration on the Digital Sky Platform and compliance with no-fly zones [w:1][w:2]; BrickByte states it uses certified remote pilots [c:677mkuk].

## 9. Risks & Challenges

Key risks include: (1) Real-estate cycles directly affect new site starts, making growth lumpy [c:q6ewrkd]; (2) Drone regulations and no-fly zones near airports limit site coverage [c:q6ewrkd][w:1]; (3) Operations-heavy delivery (drone flights, processing) keeps gross margins at 64%, below pure-software benchmarks [c:q6ewrkd]; (4) Few Indian developers maintain up-to-date BIM models, reducing the core value proposition [c:q6ewrkd]; (5) The tranche-based raise (40% at close, 30% at 150 sites, 30% at Rs 3 crore ARR) creates execution pressure and funding risk if milestones are missed [c:r542uqa]; (6) Competitors like Procore/DroneDeploy and Skylark Drones have deeper resources and can replicate BIM-comparison features [c:2lspiuh][w:8][w:14].

## 10. Investment Thesis

BrickByte addresses a genuine pain point in Indian construction: manual progress reporting that lags site reality by 2-4 weeks [c:4kixigp]. Its product—weekly drone scans compared with BIM models—is used by 23 paying customers with 126% NRR, indicating early product-market fit [c:towvifa][c:nkfzqiz]. The team combines civil engineering, computer vision, and drone operations expertise [c:uifebyv]. However, the market sizing (TAM Rs 1,600 crore, SAM Rs 300 crore) is company-reported and unverified [c:uypjwak], and the business model is operations-heavy, limiting margin expansion. The moat is thin: the BIM-comparison engine and dataset are execution advantages, not durable barriers, especially as Procore/DroneDeploy enters the Indian market [w:8][w:10]. At a Rs 38 crore post-money valuation, the company is priced for significant growth that is not yet proven at scale.

## 11. Recommendation

**Hold (5.6/10)**. BrickByte shows solid early traction with 2x ARR growth, positive unit economics, and a complete founding team. However, the operations-heavy model, thin moat, and reliance on company-reported market data cap the upside. The tranche-based raise adds execution risk. Investors should wait for evidence of sustained growth beyond 61 sites and independent validation of market size before committing.
